sections.title: Mode describes work; role describes permissions
sections.text:
1C:Enterprise mode runs an application. Users open lists, enter records, build reports and perform permitted operations. Designer supports development and administration: metadata, modules, forms and maintenance operations. Being able to open Designer does not establish that every change is safe. Access, competence and agreed scope are different questions.
A role determines permitted application operations. A form may hide a button for convenience, but a hidden button alone does not prove access control. Training edition omits some authentication mechanisms. We can study least privilege, while full sign-in and user-separation checks require an environment that actually supports them.
Distinguish modes by the task: change how the application is built, or work with its data. Adding a new kind of customer information belongs in Designer. Entering a particular customer into an existing catalog belongs in Enterprise mode. Do not select a more powerful mode merely because a familiar button is missing: first establish whether the required object exists at all.

sections.title: Three classes of change
sections.text:
Changing data means entering an invented request or fixing its description. A user setting changes a filter or column selection when the application exposes that option. Configuration changes add an attribute to the request type, change its type or introduce an event handler. The distinction follows the effect, not the number of clicks. A single Designer action may affect the structure of every record.
Suppose a consultant wants only open requests. If an existing filter supports this, a setting is enough. Storing a closure reason absent from the model may need a configuration change. Do not start by adding a field: first check whether an existing attribute already serves the purpose, how it is filled and which reports use it. This avoids unnecessary complexity.
A visible command and permission to perform an operation are different things. Hiding a button is not independent access protection: professional applications must enforce permissions where operations execute. This introductory lab changes no real account permissions and probes no third-party roles. Identify the intended operator or developer and choose the appropriate mode of your own infobase.

sections.title: Development has its own lifecycle
sections.text:
An edited working configuration and the database configuration are different states. Saving an application definition does not ensure that a running session already uses the new rule. A developer checks the change, updates the database configuration and separately verifies execution. A1 establishes this sequence; hands-on configuration starts in A4.
Before an update, preserve a recoverable copy. Changing an attribute type can affect stored values; an empty-looking form does not establish preservation. Agree on expected effects, then verify existing records, negative cases and recovery on a copy. The interactive diagram illustrates this process without performing an update.
The training edition may permit only one session. Open one mode, finish observing and close it before opening the other. A busy-infobase message does not justify deleting lock files or terminating every 1C process: someone else may have unsaved work. First check your own application window and save any changes that you actually intend to keep.

sections.title: Hand off a reproducible task
sections.text:
A useful developer request contains context, expected behavior, observed behavior and reproduction steps. “1C is broken” does not identify a test. “Filtering Status = New in the learning infobase also shows REQ-002 with status In progress” provides a checkable case. Include a synthetic example and state whether the problem remains after clearing other filters.
Do not send passwords, licensing details or a full production archive. Our course needs only a synthetic set, platform version, configuration name and chosen mode. When a task exceeds your authority, preserve a reproducible example and stop the change. This is a professional outcome, not a failure.
Your Nexus account and an infobase user are separate identities. Signing into Nexus gives access to course material and your local state; it does not create users in installed 1C. Opening a training application without a password does not demonstrate the security of a professional infobase. State which observations you made and which permissions remain untested.

sections.title: The configuration shapes the interface
sections.text:
Sections, commands and forms differ between applications. A universal instruction such as “press the third button on the left” ages quickly. Identify the purpose: a request list shows records, a request form shows one object, a report processes selected data. An empty list can indicate no records, a filter or restricted access. Test these hypotheses separately.
A1 provides a Nexus model with three requests. It supports learning to read rows and totals on a phone without an installed platform. The model is explicitly labeled and is not a 1C window. An actual empty infobase contains none of these documents; do not search for menus its configuration has not defined.
Start with three clues: the selected startup-list entry, the launch mode and the open window title. A command can move on screen while its purpose stays the same. Record the application, command and expected change rather than merely “click on the left”. Such instructions remain reproducible when window size or interface language changes.

sections.title: Catalogs, documents and references
sections.text:
Catalogs commonly hold relatively stable domain objects such as customers and services. Documents commonly represent events or operations over time. This is a useful starting point, while exact behavior remains configuration-specific. “Alpha” is a customer presentation; the relation should preserve object identity, not merely a copied name string. Two customers can share a presentation.
REQ-001 and REQ-003 refer to one invented customer. Renaming that customer should not create a second identity. Repeatedly typing names instead of retaining references causes inconsistent spelling and grouping. A2 examines items and references in the official environment; here, learn to recognize the relationship in a data set.
Customers can refer to a catalog definition, its list of items or one open card. Designer selects the object type. In Enterprise mode, a list displays multiple records and a card displays one item. Before the catalog is defined, neither its customer list nor its cards should exist. Do not fill in an arbitrary window merely because it contains a text field.

sections.title: Filters change the visible set
sections.text:
Search helps locate a record; a filter specifies membership conditions. Conditions can combine, so record every active restriction before diagnosing a result. Status = New selects only REQ-001. Customer = Alpha selects REQ-001 and REQ-003. Durations total 105 minutes for all requests and 60 for Alpha. These are arithmetic control values, not measured service productivity.
A zero-valued row and no row are different observations. A report omitting closed requests does not prove deletion. Remove filters, locate the source document and inspect report settings first. Sorting changes presentation order; it does not by itself change the sum of selected values.
Navigation history can return to a previously opened form, but it is not a data backup. Closing a form tab does not necessarily delete its object; persistence depends on the write command that was performed. This introductory exercise enters no cards. We identify context and close our own windows without changes; writing and reopening records are checked separately later.

sections.title: Verify a user scenario
sections.text:
Start with known input data and a goal, such as finding Alpha’s requests and explaining their states. Verify identifiers as well as row count: two wrong records still produce a count of two. Then inspect an empty selection to distinguish no results from a loading error.
Model controls select statuses and show request details. This trains navigation without persisting 1C data. Candidate notes are separate per course; moving to P does not automatically award A1 completion. Identify the observation source in your protocol: Nexus model or official platform.
When an interface differs from an illustration, compare meaningful landmarks: mode, object name, selected command and result. Do not force an empty infobase to display identical panels. To request help, provide these landmarks and the lesson step. License numbers, other people’s records and full-desktop screenshots are unnecessary for explaining navigation.

sections.title: Isolation starts with the path
sections.text:
A learning infobase needs its own directory and a clear name. Do not select an arbitrary infobase from a shared list. Before creating it, verify that the target directory is new and the source work remains intact. Never restore over an existing infobase. Isolation protects working data from learning mistakes and makes the experiment repeatable.
Use the platform startup window to add a new infobase without a configuration. Empty state is expected in A1. The supplied native probe instead creates a separate workspace, loads original Nexus metadata and executes BSL. Creating an infobase alone does not establish that a complete service application exists.
A learner has at least two different results: configuration and records in installed 1C, plus completion marks and notes in Nexus. Backing up one does not transfer the other. An infobase dump file, .dt, restores the 1C infobase; it is not a certificate and contains no Nexus course progress. Saving source in Studio is not a complete infobase backup either.

sections.title: Know what a copy preserves
sections.text:
Configuration sources describe structure and code. They do not back up particular customers or documents. An infobase dump transfers its state, but usefulness is established by restoring elsewhere and inspecting the result. A file with the expected extension is weak evidence by itself.
Copying an active file infobase can capture inconsistent state. Close sessions first and follow the official dump/restore workflow. Do not keep Designer and a training-edition user session open together because the edition allows only one session. Preserve earlier attempts: a new test should not destroy evidence of the previous failure.
Give each dump a new descriptive name with a date or purpose. For example, Before_change_01.dt and After_check_02.dt are different files. A file’s existence does not prove that it can be restored. Test it by loading a specifically created empty infobase and comparing expected objects and records. The original remains unchanged during this experiment.

sections.title: Copying between trajectories
sections.text:
Moving from A to P creates new work with a new ID and source provenance. Content may be copied, but completion, test results and assessment from the source trajectory are not awarded. The candidate applies this mechanism only to local learning notes; an actual infobase must be copied separately with official tools.
Record source course, target course, new ID, date and synthetic-data status. Edit the new note and reopen the source. If the original text also changes, you have shared a reference or overwritten it rather than making an independent copy. The software model needs a deep copy; infobase work needs a separate restore destination.
A .cf configuration file and a .dt infobase dump serve different purposes. Type definitions without user records do not replace a data backup. Use the infobase dump command in Designer’s Administration menu for this lesson. Our empty infobase has no customer records yet: expect to restore an empty training application, not to acquire completed course examples.

sections.title: Acceptance and its limits
sections.text:
A1 acceptance includes explaining layers, modes and objects, a navigation protocol, a separate infobase and evidence that the source survives. Nexus completion is learner self-report, not a protected exam. Author automation demonstrates a particular probe on a specified version, not a learner’s personal performance.
Without the official platform, theory, diagrams, questions and notes remain available offline. Leave the native lab unattested. You may enter P1 directly: A is not a mandatory prerequisite for P. Before continuing, preserve the environment record, control results and explicitly untested items.
Finish by reopening the original and checking that you did not accidentally continue work in the copy. Give the copy its own visible startup name. For later experiments, record which work it came from and why it was created. A short human-readable note is enough; a complex JSON protocol is not a beginner prerequisite. Keep a failed attempt alongside its correction when it explains your conclusion.

sections.title: Why a service desk needs a customer catalog
sections.text:
Imagine a dispatcher receiving service requests. Typing each customer name again invites spelling differences and accidental duplicates. A catalog lets you save a customer once and later select that record in requests. We are not creating requests yet: the small goal is a clear customer list with a record you can find after closing its window. All names in the exercise are fictional.
In 1C a catalog defines records of the same kind. Клиенты is the kind of data; «Учебный Север» is one particular catalog item. A developer defines the available properties in Designer. A user fills those properties for a particular item in 1C:Enterprise mode. Creating a catalog definition and entering a customer are therefore different activities in different modes.
A list form displays several customers; an item form, called a customer card in this lesson, displays one. Create (Создать) opens a new card. Double-clicking a saved row opens an existing one. This matters when correcting a name: selecting Create again starts another customer instead of correcting the saved record.

sections.title: What Code and Description mean
sections.text:
Our simple configuration has the standard Code (Код) and Description (Наименование) attributes. Description is text intended for people; enter «Учебный Север». Code helps distinguish rows. This lab uses automatic numbering, so leave the new code empty and inspect the value assigned when saving. Do not copy another record’s code or assume that every configuration uses the same numbering rules.
A visible field belongs to a form. An attribute is the data property whose value the field helps a user enter. For example, the Наименование field edits the Наименование attribute. The platform can generate forms for this simple catalog, so you need not design an entire window before entering the first record. A later lesson explains custom forms after you understand the user’s required actions.
Text visible in an open new card is not sufficient proof of durable saving. Choose Save and close (Записать и закрыть), wait for the list and check that a row appears. Open it again and inspect the value. Reopening distinguishes saved data from text that was merely displayed in an input. Do not close the entire application immediately after pressing Save without checking its result.

sections.title: One record, a new description: avoid an accidental duplicate
sections.text:
A saved item has its own identity. A reference allows the application to point to that item; its displayed description is only a human-readable representation. Open the existing customer, change «Учебный Север» to «Учебный Север — ремонт» and save. You are editing the same card. In this lab confirm that its code is unchanged and no additional list row has appeared.
Create starts a different workflow: a new card becomes a separate record when saved. Calling it «Учебный Север» does not automatically combine it with another customer. Our simple training catalog deliberately does not enforce unique descriptions. Search and compare available attributes before adding a new customer. A real application’s duplicate detection rules are a separate design decision.
Similar row text alone cannot prove reference equality. For now use the observable difference: renaming an existing customer leaves one row with its previous code, whereas creating «Учебный Юг» adds a second row with its own code. Programming with references and documents comes later. This introductory lab requires no GUID inspection or service identifier processing.

sections.title: An empty list, search and reopening
sections.text:
An empty visible list does not always mean data loss. You may have opened another catalog or infobase, or retained a search filter. After renaming a customer, searching for its complete old description may no longer match it. Clear the search and inspect the full list. Sorting changes row order; filters change visible membership. Neither action alone creates or deletes customers.
To check saving, close 1C:Enterprise mode and reopen the same training infobase from the launcher. Verify its displayed name and directory. Open Клиенты, clear search and find both rows. Reopen each card. If both descriptions and their separate codes are present, the reopening check has succeeded. Preserve a screenshot containing only the fictional training data.
Nexus provides the route and stores your own completion report. It does not see the external 1C window and cannot automatically confirm that your card appeared. Preserve the actual infobase and observations separately. Use the platform’s .dt dump for backup and another new infobase for restoration checks. Creating a copy must not replace the original training work.

sections.text:
Validate a request: notice an error before accepting a write
Check required fields and duration, correct a rejected new request and verify persistence by reopening it.
1c-enterprise.a 2; A1–A2: separate infobase, catalogs, references and documents; synthetic data only.

sections.title: A filled field must have the intended meaning
sections.text:
A request links a customer, service, duration and work status. A visible customer label alone does not establish a link to the intended record. Select through the list and check its code. Do not create a duplicate just because a search hides the original; clear the search first.
Field types and business rules are separate. A numeric field does not make every number an acceptable duration. Our original training document permits 0 through 1440 minutes inclusive and requires a customer, service and status. These are this configuration’s rules, not universal rules of every 1C application.

sections.title: A rejection asks you to correct the form
sections.text:
Записать triggers validation and document rules. Missing customer or service produces a prompt to select them; a missing status produces its own prompt; an out-of-range duration produces the 0..1440 message. Clicking the button alone is not a successful write.
Keep the new form open, read the reason and correct the relevant field. Do not select a random record merely to remove the message. If the result is unclear, record your steps and observation. Do not alter validation code to bypass a rejected input.

sections.title: Boundaries explain the rule
sections.text:
Compare ordinary input 30, permitted boundaries 0 and 1440, and invalid -1 and 1441. Zero is explicitly known zero effort here, not an unknown duration. A different organization may require a strictly positive duration; learn its rule instead of transferring this one automatically.

A number taken from your saved form identifies your particular request. The Поиск (Ctrl+F) box searches the displayed set under platform rules. It neither creates records nor changes customer links. Check the search text and active restrictions before assuming a request is missing.
Search may operate within an already restricted period or filtered set. An empty result is not evidence of deleted data. Clear the search, disable your filter and check the period, then compare the infobase and actual number.

The condition checkbox controls whether it applies. Its text and value may remain visible while unchecked: the setting is retained but no longer restricts rows. This allows reversible comparison without deleting either records or the setting.

sections.text:
Search text, a period and a duration filter can apply together. Searching the number of a 30-minute request while ≥45 is active gives an empty set. Understand the intersection instead of creating the request again. Change one restriction at a time and record what restores the row.
Advanced И and ИЛИ groups mean all conditions and at least one condition respectively. Start with one numeric condition. For an additional experiment predict the matching numbers manually before combining conditions. A list setting changes neither document validation rules nor access permissions.

Clicking the numeric column header changes list order; another click switches direction. Check actual values rather than guessing a small arrow’s meaning. For 30, 45, 30 and 15, ascending order is 15, 30, 30, 45; descending is 45, 30, 30, 15.
Document numbers and fields do not change. The second row after sorting may be a different request. Identify your document by its actual number. Equal durations do not guarantee a particular relative order without an additional sort criterion.

sections.title: Grouping puts related details under a heading
sections.text:
Grouping by Клиент places requests linked to the same customer under one heading. This uses a customer reference rather than similar text. Two same-named customer records can form different groups; investigate identity before changing names for cosmetic consistency.
A plus beside a group expands its details. A collapsed group does not imply missing or deleted documents. Its heading is not an additional request: count document numbers rather than visible bands.

sections.title: Order, group and aggregate are different
sections.text:
Sorting chooses order, grouping organizes related details and filtering chooses which rows are included. They can act together. Disable your duration filter before sorting, otherwise excluded values remain hidden. Grouped presentation can also affect where a sort is applied.
A normal list grouping does not promise an automatic duration total in the heading. The next lesson’s separate report calculates count and minutes as aggregates. Here reconcile numbers and manually calculate 105 minutes for the first customer and 15 for the second.

lessons.title: Customer report: turn source documents into a verifiable total

sections.title: Customer report: turn source documents into a verifiable total
sections.text:
Customer report: turn source documents into a verifiable total
Generate the prepared report in your training infobase, reconcile counts and minutes with source requests and explain a customer filter.
1c-enterprise.a 2; A1–A2: separate infobase, catalogs, references and documents; synthetic data only.
Locate the actual prepared report rather than assume a universal report exists.
Reconcile overall and customer totals with an independent table of numbers.
Disable the filter, regenerate and confirm that original requests remain intact.

sections.title: A report reads documents without replacing them
sections.text:
The training package includes Заявки по клиентам. It reads ЗаявкаУслуги documents, excludes deletion-marked records and groups by customer reference. Количество counts included requests; Минуты sums ДлительностьМинут. Generating a report writes no request documents. A report row is not another document.
This simple variant has no period or status restriction: all non-deletion-marked requests are included, including Новая. Do not import assumptions from another application. A universal report is not automatically present in every empty infobase; this is a specific report supplied with our original training package.

sections.title: Prepare the control before generating
sections.text:
From the previous lesson record each actual number, customer and duration. The sequential dataset has Учебный Север — ремонт with 30, 45 and 30 minutes and Учебный Юг with 15. Expected totals: first customer 3 and 105; second 1 and 15; overall 4 and 120. Include additional requests you created rather than deleting them to match an illustration.
Derive the control from the primary list and opened documents, not a copy of the report under test. Equal sums do not prove equal composition: 30+45 and 15+60 both yield 75 but represent different requests. Check count, customer reference, numbers and units together.

sections.title: Parameters and a fresh result are separate states
sections.text:
Open Учебная сервисная служба → Отчёты → Заявки по клиентам. Disable the Клиент checkbox and choose Сформировать. After changing its value or checkbox, choose Сформировать again: the previous result can remain visible until regeneration.
For the customer restriction enable Клиент and select the existing Учебный Север — ремонт catalog item. It is a reference to an item, not a search for similar text. Equally named items may have different codes and separate totals. Do not create another customer merely to filter the report.

sections.title: Why 120 and 105 can both be correct
sections.text:
The overall report includes four requests and 120 minutes. The first-customer restriction includes three and 105. The difference of 15 belongs to the second customer; it is a change of scope, not lost data. Disabling the checkbox and regenerating should restore 4 and 120 without editing documents.
When results disagree, compare scope before composition. Check Клиент, the selected item and regeneration. In the primary list clear your restrictions and compare numbers, minutes and deletion marks. Do not change data to obtain an attractive total or remove other deletion marks: retain the discrepancy and identify the included or omitted request.

sections.title: When the report command is absent
sections.text:
First check that you opened the same infobase used for earlier labs. The current prepared package already includes the report, so loading another configuration over your work is unnecessary. An earlier package may lack it. In that case use the additional copy-update route below while retaining the original infobase separately.
That route applies to the unchanged Nexus training structure when only data was added. Loading a full .cf over your custom objects or code can replace that development: stop, preserve the base and review merging separately. A .cf contains configuration structure and training code, not a backup of your documents. A .dt export contains the infobase configuration and data.

sections.title: What constitutes the lab result
sections.text:
Keep your control table, the parameters of three generations and observations: all → first customer → all. Reopen one earlier request by number and verify its customer and minutes. Illustrations use synthetic Учебный клиент А and Б from a separate test; your names, dates and numbers can differ.
Nexus can store your self-reported completion and a safe result description. That is not a server-side BSL verdict or proof of authorship. This lab runs in installed 1C; Studio, source transfer and Windows Sandbox are unnecessary.

sections.title: Optional: preserve an earlier package in a separate copy
sections.text:
Use this section only when the report is absent and your infobase has the earlier unchanged Nexus training structure. If you added objects or changed configuration code, do not load a full .cf: preserve a .dt and review merging separately. The normal current-package workflow needs none of these steps.
1. Close this infobase’s Enterprise window. Select the original training infobase in the launcher and open Конфигуратор. Choose Администрирование → Выгрузить информационную базу…, save a clearly named .dt backup in a separate folder and wait for successful completion. Do not continue after a failed export. Close Designer.
2. In the launcher choose Добавить → create a new infobase → without configuration. Give it a distinct name, such as My service — report copy, and a new separate folder. Open Designer for the NEW base, verify its identity and choose Администрирование → Загрузить информационную базу… using your .dt. Restoration replaces its target, so that target must be only the new empty copy. Retain the original launcher entry.

sections.title: Optional: add the report only to that prepared copy

3. Open the restored new copy in Enterprise and compare previous numbers and fields with your control table. Stop and return to the original when they differ; do not edit documents to hide a mismatch. Close Enterprise.

Settings or development: choose the appropriate change
Distinguish a personal list setting from a structural configuration change and justify a minimal solution.

sections.title: Clarify the observable need
sections.text:
Make customers easier to use is not a complete specification. Ask whether the person needs to find an existing item, change a caption or store new text per customer. Those tasks use different mechanisms. Record an action and an observable acceptance result.
Our next task is precise: store a short training note separately from each customer name. It must survive writing and reopening the same item. Use synthetic information only; never put passwords, personal or business data in this field.

sections.title: Settings present existing data differently
sections.text:
A ≥45 filter selects requests, sorting changes order and grouping gathers details. They use existing fields without creating a Клиенты attribute or changing document storage structure. Disable the filter and compare original numbers to prove reversibility.
A setting may be saved per user and variant, but verify its actual scope in the application. Do not claim a personal filter changes all users. A visible column alone does not prove new storage; it might expose an existing field. Inspect metadata first.

sections.title: Names, synonyms and values serve different roles
sections.text:
In Designer open Справочники → Клиенты → Основные. Имя Клиенты participates in code such as Справочники.Клиенты. Синоним is its readable label. Учебный Север — ремонт is one Enterprise item’s name. Confusing these levels causes unnecessary changes.
A synonym change does not create another catalog; renaming an item does not add a field. A note needs a string attribute. Another application could offer an additional-attributes mechanism, but this small original package does not promise one. Do not search indefinitely or introduce third-party development for this exercise.

sections.title: Decide who owns the value
sections.text:
The note describes one customer independently of requests, so it belongs to a Клиенты item. Putting it in a document would give separate notes to that customer’s different requests. That can be another valid need, but is not ours. Do not create another customer entity for one field.
In the prepared structure Клиенты has no custom attributes; Код and Наименование are standard properties. Use Add in Реквизиты rather than Табличные части. A tabular section stores multiple rows inside one object and is excessive here.

sections.title: A technical name and readable synonym
sections.text:
Use the technical name УчебнаяЗаметка without spaces. Its synonym Учебная заметка is displayed in the form. The platform may derive the synonym automatically when you leave the name field; still verify it. A synonym change does not alter the purpose or type of stored values.
If the attribute exists from an earlier attempt, inspect and reuse it instead of adding УчебнаяЗаметка1. Prior work and attempt history matter more than matching an illustration. Resolve a different meaning behind an identical name before proceeding.

Leave unlimited length disabled. Check the new attribute’s right-hand Длина, not the standard Наименование length in the central editor.
Choose limits from need and boundary examples. Plan empty, ordinary, exactly 80-character and over-limit inputs. Do not promise a specific over-limit message: a form may constrain input before writing. Observe actual behavior and compare the persisted length.

Earlier items initially have empty notes until filled. The attribute is optional, so this update does not require rewriting every old customer. An empty note does not mean a missing name, code or reference. Mandatory input and default filling are separate rules introduced deliberately.
Close the object editor and save the configuration. This saves the development description. sections.title: An entity follows its lifecycle

A customer exists before and after individual requests; a service describes an offering; a request records an occurrence in time. Catalogs represent reusable entities; documents represent individual requests. One customer can have many requests and one service many customers. Test that multiplicity synthetically. Usable forms do not replace write rules. Invalid minutes must reject through alternative input routes, and correcting one field must preserve other input. sections.title: Roles and least privilege
sections.text:
Roles and least privilege
Build a least-privilege matrix and test allowed and denied operations.
1c-enterprise.a 5; A1–A2: separate infobase, catalogs, references and documents; synthetic data only.
Build a least-privilege matrix and test allowed and denied operations.

sections.title: Roles describe capabilities
sections.text:
An operator creates and reads requests; a consultant configures variants; a developer changes configuration. These are teaching roles, not a complete production policy. Specify object, action and data scope per operation. Full access for everyone hides the symptom rather than solving responsibility boundaries.
Begin administration with responsibility boundaries: operators correct input, developers algorithms, and administrators the permitted environment/recovery. Being able to execute a command does not authorize consequences. Record purpose, source, destination and prohibited changes before acting; record outcome and preservation afterwards. This turns potentially dangerous clicks into a controlled experiment with an explicit acceptance condition.

sections.title: Visibility is not permission
sections.text:
Hiding a command can improve UI, but denial must apply to the operation. Another list or programmatic route must not bypass the rule. Denying everything is also incorrect. Alongside each denial, test a necessary allowed operation for the same role.
A full backup restores data, not merely earlier code. Preserve platform/configuration versions, control identities and totals. Restore only to a fresh destination without someone else’s work. File existence is insufficient: open the restored instance and confirm accepted state survives another session. Recovery evidence names what was checked rather than implying every function was covered.

sections.title: A check has an environment
sections.text:
Training edition limits authentication and simultaneous sessions. It can teach role structure and scenarios but does not establish a complete multi-user security PASS. Execute the matrix in a permitted environment with separate teaching users. Never use real credentials or publish a password to simplify reproduction.
Permission tests must allow required work while denying excess. Login failure alone is not an object-permission test. Pair each negative attempt with an allowed control in a suitable environment. Record training limitations separately: one-user login does not prove multi-user separation or authorize production use. Keep credentials out of logs and use synthetic roles/data.

sections.title: Denial preserves state
sections.text:
An operator may not change schema or delete a catalog. Record state before the attempt, observed denial and state afterwards. Login failure does not prove object permissions: first authenticate as the intended role and execute an allowed workflow. Distinguish environment failure, permission denial and business validation.
Preserve observations before testing hypotheses. Changing version, role and data together destroys causal explanation. Hand off minimal reproduction and sanitized classification while keeping private logs restricted. Repeat the original case and preservation control after fixing. Record failed attempts before cleanup: they can explain accepted limitations and prevent another unsafe experiment.

Backup and restore
Restore data and configuration into a new infobase and prove source preservation.
1c-enterprise.a 5; A1–A2: separate infobase, catalogs, references and documents; synthetic data only.
Restore data and configuration into a new infobase and prove source preservation.

sections.title: A backup contains state
sections.text:
A configuration export describes the solution but is not a full copy of customer documents. An infobase dump preserves data with configuration in its supported format. Copying an open file directory can be inconsistent. Choose a supported method and ensure the required absence of active writes.
Begin administration with responsibility boundaries: operators correct input, developers algorithms, and administrators the permitted environment/recovery. Being able to execute a command does not authorize consequences. Record purpose, source, destination and prohibited changes before acting; record outcome and preservation afterwards. This turns potentially dangerous clicks into a controlled experiment with an explicit acceptance condition.

sections.title: A file is not a verified restore
sections.text:
Creating a backup file does not prove usability. Restore it into a fresh empty directory, open it and reconcile identities, count, totals and configuration version. File size or extension alone cannot detect the wrong source or a logically incomplete copy.
A full backup restores data, not merely earlier code. Preserve platform/configuration versions, control identities and totals. Restore only to a fresh destination without someone else’s work. File existence is insufficient: open the restored instance and confirm accepted state survives another session. Recovery evidence names what was checked rather than implying every function was covered.

sections.title: The source is never the target
sections.text:
Record source and fresh destination paths before the operation. If the destination exists, choose another; never erase it automatically. After restore, change the copy to 90 minutes and reread the 75-minute source. This proves independent working instances rather than two shortcuts to one infobase.
Permission tests must allow required work while denying excess. Login failure alone is not an object-permission test. Pair each negative attempt with an allowed control in a suitable environment. Record training limitations separately: one-user login does not prove multi-user separation or authorize production use. Keep credentials out of logs and use synthetic roles/data.

sections.title: Rejection also needs a protocol
sections.text:
A damaged or unsuitable file should produce explicit rejection. Do not repair the only backup in place or test it by overwriting work. Preserve a file copy, a safe error classification and unchanged source. A recovery plan also identifies storage, acceptable loss of recent changes and responsibility for verification.
Preserve observations before testing hypotheses. Changing version, role and data together destroys causal explanation. Hand off minimal reproduction and sanitized classification while keeping private logs restricted. Repeat the original case and preservation control after fixing. Record failed attempts before cleanup: they can explain accepted limitations and prevent another unsafe experiment.

sections.title: Platform and solution updates differ
sections.text:
A new executable platform version and a new configuration are different changes. Record both versions, compatibility mode and purpose before and after. Do not blame every error on “old 1C” without reproduction. Start with one configuration change on the same platform to avoid mixing two factors.
Begin administration with responsibility boundaries: operators correct input, developers algorithms, and administrators the permitted environment/recovery. Being able to execute a command does not authorize consequences. Record purpose, source, destination and prohibited changes before acting; record outcome and preservation afterwards. This turns potentially dangerous clicks into a controlled experiment with an explicit acceptance condition.

sections.title: A control dataset protects meaning
sections.text:
Prepare an old request, a new request, zero duration and rejected input. Reconcile report and references before upgrading. Repeat the same set afterwards and add the new capability’s scenario. Opening the main window is insufficient: lost fields or broken filters may appear only when old data is read.
A full backup restores data, not merely earlier code. Preserve platform/configuration versions, control identities and totals. Restore only to a fresh destination without someone else’s work. File existence is insufficient: open the restored instance and confirm accepted state survives another session. Recovery evidence names what was checked rather than implying every function was covered.

sections.title: Verify return beforehand
sections.text:
Back up before changing and verify restoration separately. Once an upgrade changes data, replacing the executable alone need not restore earlier state. Keep source and upgraded copies with distinct paths and identities. Preserve failed copies until the cause and safe protocol have been recorded.
Permission tests must allow required work while denying excess. Login failure alone is not an object-permission test. Pair each negative attempt with an allowed control in a suitable environment. Record training limitations separately: one-user login does not prove multi-user separation or authorize production use. Keep credentials out of logs and use synthetic roles/data.

sections.title: Apply based on results
sections.text:
The summary lists passed, failed and untested workflows plus rollback. Untested exchange or permissions do not inherit PASS from unrelated checks. The teaching task delivers a tested candidate rather than publishing it. Real working-system changes require their owner and an agreed maintenance window even after successful tests.
Preserve observations before testing hypotheses. Changing version, role and data together destroys causal explanation. Hand off minimal reproduction and sanitized classification while keeping private logs restricted. Repeat the original case and preservation control after fixing. Record failed attempts before cleanup: they can explain accepted limitations and prevent another unsafe experiment.

Diagnosis and escalation
Prepare a reproducible support request without data leakage or dangerous repairs.
1c-enterprise.a 5; A1–A2: separate infobase, catalogs, references and documents; synthetic data only.
Prepare a reproducible support request without data leakage or dangerous repairs.

sections.title: Separate symptom from hypothesis
sections.text:
“R1 does not save after−1” is an observation;“the infobase is broken” is a hypothesis. Record expectation, safe reproduction steps, version and outcome. Reproduce on a synthetic copy. Do not attach real data publicly when the issue occurs only there; prepare a minimal sanitized example and agree on access separately.
Begin administration with responsibility boundaries: operators correct input, developers algorithms, and administrators the permitted environment/recovery. Being able to execute a command does not authorize consequences. Record purpose, source, destination and prohibited changes before acting; record outcome and preservation afterwards. This turns potentially dangerous clicks into a controlled experiment with an explicit acceptance condition.

sections.title: Classification narrows diagnosis
sections.text:
Distinguish business-rule rejection, permission denial, configuration defect, environment unavailability and persistence failure. A generic “error” does not prescribe a fix. Compare valid and invalid inputs and inspect state. Do not change role, platform and data simultaneously: the cause of improvement becomes unknowable.
A full backup restores data, not merely earlier code. Preserve platform/configuration versions, control identities and totals. Restore only to a fresh destination without someone else’s work. File existence is insufficient: open the restored instance and confirm accepted state survives another session. Recovery evidence names what was checked rather than implying every function was covered.

sections.title: Provide the minimum sufficient package
sections.text:
Include case ID, time, versions, expected/actual, safe message excerpt and control total. Exclude passwords, tokens, full databases and third-party configurations. Review screenshots before sharing. Restrict technical logs; publish only necessary classification and a synthetic example.
Permission tests must allow required work while denying excess. Login failure alone is not an object-permission test. Pair each negative attempt with an allowed control in a suitable environment. Record training limitations separately: one-user login does not prove multi-user separation or authorize production use. Keep credentials out of logs and use synthetic roles/data.

sections.title: Bound independent repairs
sections.text:
An operator may correct input under a clear rule, but must not run unknown processors or mass cleanup. Preserve work and contact the responsible role. After a fix, repeat the original case and a nearby positive control. Closing the ticket without retesting does not prove the issue disappeared or data survived.
Preserve observations before testing hypotheses. Changing version, role and data together destroys causal explanation. Hand off minimal reproduction and sanitized classification while keeping private logs restricted. Repeat the original case and preservation control after fixing. Record failed attempts before cleanup: they can explain accepted limitations and prevent another unsafe experiment.

sections.title: Standard report parameters
sections.text:
Standard report parameters
Set report parameters and distinguish data-selection conditions from presentation.
1c-enterprise.a 6; A1–A2: separate infobase, catalogs, references and documents; synthetic data only.
Set report parameters and distinguish data-selection conditions from presentation.

sections.title: The question determines parameters
sections.text:
For a request report, specify period, customer and status. Color, column width and order do not replace those conditions. Record values before generating the report. Using today’s date instead of a fixed period makes a teaching result irreproducible.
Start reports from a testable question, not a layout. Name period, customer, status, resource and units, then list expected document identities. Sum, row count and group count answer different questions. Without this distinction, a plausible setting can answer the wrong question. A small independent table lets reviewers identify the first mismatch rather than guessing from appearance.

sections.title: Resources have units
sections.text:
Minutes, document count and cost are different resources. A total 90 is meaningless without a label. Cost needs rate and rounding rules; it is not the sum of minutes. Keep units explicit, reconcile a small set manually, and introduce another resource as a separate agreed change.
Saved variants preserve available settings, not necessarily a frozen dataset. New documents can change results. Archive parameters, time, membership and observed totals separately. Reopen the variant itself: a familiar title can remain after a required filter was lost or experimentally changed. Compare actual settings rather than trusting names or save notifications.

sections.title: Filters can act at different levels
sections.text:
Dataset conditions and hiding an already-produced group can look similar while yielding different totals. State which records participate in calculation. Do not “fix” a wrong total by hiding result rows. Return to source document identities and verify membership before aggregation.
Distinguish settings from executing a program component. External processors can modify data and act outside an infobase; an infobase copy is not host isolation. Decline execution from unknown sources and request provenance review. Hashes prove equal bytes; security needs authority analysis and a verified execution boundary appropriate to the scenario.

sections.title: Detect wrong parameters
sections.text:
Test an ordinary period, an empty period and date boundaries. If start follows end, require clear rejection or an explicitly agreed empty result. Accidental behavior is not a rule. Preserve parameters and expected identities with the result; a total screenshot alone cannot reproduce the calculation.
End consulting with reproducible explanation. Parameter discrepancies need setting corrections; missing fields/algorithms need a development request. Share expected/actual, steps and tested causes without secrets or real infobases. Repeat the workflow after changes. A closed ticket is not acceptance and does not turn untested permissions or exports intoPASS.

sections.title: A variant stores settings
sections.text:
A report variant stores available parameters, filters, groupings and presentation; it need not store a frozen dataset. A new request can change the result of an old variant. Label purpose and fixed versus dynamic parameters so users do not mistake saved settings for an archived result.
Start reports from a testable question, not a layout. Name period, customer, status, resource and units, then list expected document identities. Sum, row count and group count answer different questions. Without this distinction, a plausible setting can answer the wrong question. A small independent table lets reviewers identify the first mismatch rather than guessing from appearance.

sections.title: Names should identify the workflow
sections.text:
“Alpha/open/training-period” is clearer than “MyReport2.” Specify owner and personal/shared scope. Changing a shared variant affects others and needs checking. Create another variant for experiments instead of overwriting the accepted one. This preserves comparison and return paths.
Saved variants preserve available settings, not necessarily a frozen dataset. New documents can change results. Archive parameters, time, membership and observed totals separately. Reopen the variant itself: a familiar title can remain after a required filter was lost or experimentally changed. Compare actual settings rather than trusting names or save notifications.

sections.title: A processor is executable code
sections.text:
An external processor can read/change data, access files and use available platform actions. Its extension does not make it safe; nor does a familiar sender prove unchanged content. Establish author, purpose, official source and required rights before opening anything. Never execute an unknown file out of curiosity.
Start reports from a testable question, not a layout. Name period, customer, status, resource and units, then list expected document identities. Sum, row count and group count answer different questions. Without this distinction, a plausible setting can answer the wrong question. A small independent table lets reviewers identify the first mismatch rather than guessing from appearance.

sections.title: A hash binds review to a file
sections.text:
SHA256 binds a reviewed copy to later bytes; it does not itself prove harmlessness. A malicious file also has a hash. Compare against a trusted channel and attach review to that exact copy. Any modification creates new bytes requiring a new review.
Saved variants preserve available settings, not necessarily a frozen dataset. New documents can change results. Archive parameters, time, membership and observed totals separately. Reopen the variant itself: a familiar title can remain after a required filter was lost or experimentally changed. Compare actual settings rather than trusting names or save notifications.

sections.title: An infobase copy does not isolate the computer

Safe mode and rights have specific contexts; full execution isolation requires an agreed boundary and evidence, not a checkbox.
Distinguish settings from executing a program component. External processors can modify data and act outside an infobase; an infobase copy is not host isolation. Decline execution from unknown sources and request provenance review. Hashes prove equal bytes; security needs authority analysis and a verified execution boundary appropriate to the scenario.

Saved variants preserve available settings, not necessarily a frozen dataset. New documents can change results. Archive parameters, time, membership and observed totals separately. sections.text:
Start the final work from operator tasks: create a request, find open work, obtain a total and restore a copy. Screen lists do not replace requirements. Specify input, action, expectation and evidence for each scenario. Variant parameters are separate so the work is not merely replaying a solved example.
The final project transfers skills to an independent dataset. Use a new instance with permitted-template provenance and prior requirements. Entry, search, reporting and recovery form one workflow. sections.title: Acceptance includes prohibitions
sections.text:
Positive cases show usefulness; negative cases show boundaries. Include empty customer, invalid duration and attempted restore over existing work. Verify both rejection and unchanged state. A successful ordinary input after failure proves usability rather than mere action blocking.
Choose data that distinguishes defects. Multiple customers, equal labels with different identities, zero duration and varied statuses expose filter/grouping errors. Calculate expectations independently before running reports. When wrong solutions coincide numerically, add a discriminating case. Never rewrite the oracle to fit output or call an explanatory model actual 1C execution.

sections.text:
Prepare 12 synthetic requests across customers, statuses and duration boundaries. Calculate control totals manually before running reports. A teaching template may seed a new copy, but record provenance and your own changes. Never overwrite previously accepted work for a final variant.
Preservation is critical. Keep prior results, source infobase and attempts available. Restore to a fresh directory, edit only the copy and reread the source. A startup screenshot does not prove this chain. Portfolios identify versions, work IDs, control identities, expected/observed values, negative cases and environment limits. This makes independent reproduction possible without accessing private data.

sections.title: Publish criteria before work
sections.text:

Defend choices against the actual submission: field type, rejection rule and source of a total. Make a small transfer change in another copy. Declare templates and assistance honestly. A local self-report is neither instructor grading nor authorship verification. AandPare independent: a project copy can support learning without automatically transferring completion credit.

sections.title: A defense explains decisions
sections.text:
Show model, workflows, checks and recovery rather than reciting definitions. Explain field types, references versus names and rejected-write behavior. Review questions concern the actual deliverable. A local system may preserve answers as self-report but cannot call that an independent defense.
The final project transfers skills to an independent dataset. Use a new instance with permitted-template provenance and prior requirements. Entry, search, reporting and recovery form one workflow. Replace “build a system” with observable action outcomes. Screen count/archive size do not measure correctness, and a successful demonstration does not eliminate negative tests.

sections.title: A transfer change checks understanding
sections.text:
Add a filter or report variant for another period. Predict the result, create a copy and change it without a solved walkthrough. Then repeat prior workflows. Explaining the consequences of a changed condition demonstrates understanding better than replaying a memorized click sequence.
Choose data that distinguishes defects. Multiple customers, equal labels with different identities, zero duration and varied statuses expose filter/grouping errors. Calculate expectations independently before running reports. When wrong solutions coincide numerically, add a discriminating case. Never rewrite the oracle to fit output or call an explanatory model actual 1C execution.

sections.title: Transition to P is optional
sections.text:
An applied graduate operates the system and performs foundational configuration within scope. Professional P adds algorithms, modules, queries and engineering verification. Shared concepts help, but A completion does not automatically complete P topics. Transition creates a new work copy with provenance rather than transferring unrelated competency credit.
Preservation is critical. Keep prior results, source infobase and attempts available. Restore to a fresh directory, edit only the copy and reread the source. A startup screenshot does not prove this chain. Portfolios identify versions, work IDs, control identities, expected/observed values, negative cases and environment limits. This makes independent reproduction possible without accessing private data.

sections.title: The final package remains learner work
sections.text:
Preserve the pre-defense version, changed copy, answers and transfer-check results. Do not erase attempts to beautify the record. Declare templates and assistance without claiming unverified independent authorship. Instructor grading and certification belong to a separate process that local self-checking does not replace.
Defend choices against the actual submission: field type, rejection rule and source of a total. Make a small transfer change in another copy. Declare templates and assistance honestly. A local self-report is neither instructor grading nor authorship verification. AandPare independent: a project copy can support learning without automatically transferring completion credit.

terms.definition: The language used to program calculations, checks and event handlers in a 1C application. BSL is the designation used in development tools and the .bsl source extension.
terms.example: Сообщить(30 + 45); is executed by the 1C platform in an appropriate module.

terms.definition: The software used to develop and run applications. It provides forms, data storage, the script language and access control. The service desk configuration supplies its particular business rules.
terms.example: One installed platform can open several separate training infobases.

terms.definition: Definitions of application objects, forms and source modules. They determine which data and actions the application supports. The definition differs from the customer records entered by a user.
terms.example: The Клиенты catalog is defined in the configuration; «Учебный Север» is a record in an infobase.

terms.definition: One application instance containing its database configuration, entered records and service information. Separate infobases can have the same configuration but different customer records.
terms.example: Keep the practice infobase and its restored copy in different directories.

terms.definition: The platform mode used to change catalogs, attributes, forms and modules. Select the correct infobase in the launcher, then choose Designer (Конфигуратор).
terms.example: Enter the first calculation in the managed application module in Designer.

terms.definition: The mode for using an application: opening lists, entering records and viewing results. Its window differs from Designer.
terms.example: Create a customer from the Клиенты list using Create (Создать) in 1C:Enterprise mode.

terms.full: Definitions of data and application behavior
terms.definition: Definitions of application objects and their properties. A developer defines a catalog and its attributes; users enter records using that structure.
terms.example: ТарифЧас defines a service attribute; 1200 in a service record is an attribute value.

terms.full: An object for records of the same kind
terms.definition: A collection of relatively stable data, such as customers or services. Each customer is a separate item. A 1C catalog differs from this Nexus terminology reference.
terms.example: Клиенты contains the separate records «Учебный Север» and «Учебный Юг».

terms.definition: A particular customer or service saved in the infobase. You can open its form and change it. Renaming a saved item does not itself create a second customer.
terms.example: Open «Учебный Север», change its description and save that same item.

terms.full: A named property of a 1C object
terms.definition: A named property with an allowed value type. A form helps a person enter its value, but a form control and the attribute definition are different application parts.
terms.example: Наименование holds a customer description; ТарифЧас holds a numeric service rate.

terms.definition: An application screen with fields and commands. A list form displays several records; an item form edits one. The platform can generate forms for a simple catalog.
terms.example: Double-click a customer in the list to open its item form.

terms.definition: Distinguishes saved objects and connects them. An object can keep its reference when its displayed name changes. Two equal names do not prove that two records are the same customer.
terms.example: A request stores a reference to its selected customer rather than only a printed name.

terms.full: A configuration component containing source code
terms.definition: Program text executed in a particular context. Applications, forms and objects have different modules, and code available in one context may be unavailable in another.
terms.example: Place the first calculation inside ПриНачалеРаботыСистемы in the managed application module.

terms.full: A name used to hold a program value
terms.definition: Stores a value so the program can refer to it by name. Assignment evaluates its right side before updating the variable on its left. The name itself does not determine the value type.
terms.example: After Минуты = 30; the variable Минуты holds the number 30. This does not save a database record.

terms.definition: A code block executed when called. An event handler is a procedure called by the platform for a particular event. In this lab place code inside the handler rather than after КонецПроцедуры.
terms.example: ПриНачалеРаботыСистемы runs when the application starts.

terms.full: An application object representing an event
terms.definition: Stores an event, such as a dated service request for a customer. Writing a document saves its data. Posting behavior is defined separately by the application.
terms.example: ЗаявкаУслуги represents one customer service request.

terms.full: Applying a document’s defined business effects
terms.definition: A document operation that can write register records and perform checks according to the configuration. Writing and posting a document are separate actions.
terms.example: A document can be saved without being posted; inspect its state.

terms.full: Structured storage for information or accounting records
terms.definition: Choose the register kind for the problem: information registers for facts or settings, accumulation registers for balances or turnovers. Each lab explains its dimensions and resources.
terms.example: Request status history and resource balances require different storage models.

terms.definition: A separate environment for developing 1C applications. Early labs use Designer, which comes with the platform; EDT is an additional development tool.
terms.example: You do not need EDT just to create the first customer record.

terms.full: A runtime for scripts compatible with the 1C language
terms.definition: A separate scripting project. Language compatibility does not provide every 1C platform object: your infobase catalogs and documents are not automatically available.
terms.example: An .os script may run in OneScript; perform the Клиенты lab in its specified 1C environment.

terms.definition: An editor tool that analyzes source text and reports potential issues. Its diagnostics help write code; they do not mean that the code was executed in 1C.
terms.example: A style diagnostic and the actual output 75 in 1C are different results.

terms.full: Workspace — files belonging to one Nexus Studio work
terms.definition: Files and saved revisions of one work, separated from the template and other works. A source workspace is not a running 1C infobase.
terms.example: A Studio copy receives its own ID; editing it does not change the source work.

terms.definition: An application definition file, not a complete backup of infobase user data. Load a training template only into a new empty infobase as instructed to avoid replacing your own application.
terms.example: Configuration → Load configuration from file… accepts a .cf file.

terms.definition: A file created by the platform’s dump command for backup and transfer. Test restoration in another new infobase while preserving the original.
terms.example: Designer → Administration → Dump infobase… creates a .dt file.

terms.definition: A text format for structured data. Configuration source XML files describe metadata. They differ from BSL modules and from complete infobase backups.
terms.example: Catalogs/Клиенты.xml describes the catalog in a source directory.

terms.definition: A container holding files and directories. In Windows, Extract All… unpacks it. Installing software or loading an infobase is a separate action after extraction.
terms.example: Extract the downloaded distribution ZIP before running setup.exe according to the 1C instructions.

terms.definition: A text format with named properties, values and lists. Downloading JSON does not start 1C. The instructions and structure determine the purpose of each particular file.
terms.example: An isolated-check request and its execution report are separate JSON files.

terms.definition: Rules and operations that programs use to interact. The first calculation needs no external service API; integration labs use their specified training service.
terms.example: A training service can receive a request for a ticket status and return a response.

terms.definition: Rules for exchanging requests and responses between clients and servers. Interpret response status together with the response body.
terms.example: 200 usually indicates successful HTTP request handling; it does not prove that all returned data is correct.

terms.full: A description of a data selection
terms.definition: Specifies which data to retrieve and how to join or group it. The 1C query language differs from BSL; a BSL program can create a Запрос object and set its query text.
terms.example: ВЫБРАТЬ Наименование ИЗ Справочник.Клиенты is query text rather than a standalone BSL statement.

terms.definition: A language family for relational databases. The 1C query language has its own rules and uses the platform data model. These labs do not require direct SQL modifications.
terms.example: A 1C query to Справочник.Клиенты does not require knowing the DBMS physical table names.

terms.definition: The offline package supports its included lessons and self-checks without internet access. Prepare platform installers and downloads beforehand. Installed 1C performs actual code execution.
terms.example: Download the materials in advance; the package’s self-reports remain separate from the online account.

terms.definition: An optional engineering tool. Ordinary introductory labs use an installed training 1C application. Do not keep the only copy of your work inside a temporary environment.
terms.example: Sandbox temporary data disappears when it closes; preserve the source work outside it.

terms.full: Your own report of completing an activity
terms.definition: A record of your statement that you performed the steps and preserved the result. It supports learning progress but does not replace instructor review, execution evidence or authorship verification.
terms.example: Selecting the lab attestation does not mean Nexus inspected your external 1C infobase.

references.title: How to do a lab: from installation to an observed result
references.text:
How to do a lab: from installation to an observed result

Study in Nexus and do actual practical work in the official training 1C installed on your PC. Introductory labs need no Studio, JSON requests, source archives or Windows Sandbox. First check which application each step uses.

Download the original training configuration with its report (.cf)

This original training definition (.cf) includes no customer records or 1C platform. Load it only when the lesson calls for the prepared service desk, into a new empty infobase following that lesson. Initial programming exercises can use your own empty infobase without it. Double-clicking .cf does not install 1C. The package includes the original customer report for later lessons. Preserve existing work and follow the continuation instructions for your own infobase.

native/downloads/NexusTrainingServiceDeskReportsV2.cf

1. Open the task in Nexus

Nexus → the lesson → Laboratory

You have selected the intended course and topic.

Read the goal, starting conditions and expected result. Keep the lesson open. Each step identifies its application: Nexus, Designer or 1C:Enterprise.

Know where an action belongs and what observation will satisfy the task.

State the task in your own words, such as creating a customer card or obtaining a total of 75.

Do not enter code in the assistant chat instead of a 1C module. The assistant explains; the application named in the lab performs execution.

2. Obtain the official training platform

Browser → the official 1C page

An appropriate lawfully installed 1C version may already be sufficient.

Use the official training edition link below. Follow 1C’s distribution instructions and select the appropriate system version. Nexus neither includes nor resells the platform installer.

Actual execution needs the official product under appropriate terms of use.

You have the official distribution or an appropriate existing installation.

Use no unknown builds or third-party application configurations. If the selected version requires licensing, use a lawful license or the official training edition. The course provides no protection bypass.

3. Extract and install 1C

Windows → File Explorer → the 1C installer

The distribution was downloaded from its official source.

Open Downloads. For ZIP, right-click the archive → Extract All… → choose a new directory → Extract. Wait, then open the extracted directory. Locate setup.exe according to the distribution instructions and run it. Read the terms and follow the installation wizard. Do not run the installer directly inside an unextracted archive.

Extraction gives the installer access to the distribution files; a ZIP archive is not an installed application.

The 1C launcher is available from Start and opens the infobase list.

If installation is unavailable, read the system message and official requirements. Continue the theory in Nexus meanwhile; enabling Windows Sandbox is unnecessary for introductory labs.

4. Create a separate empty training infobase

The 1C:Enterprise launcher

The platform is installed; choose a new directory that contains none of your previous work.

Select Add… (Добавить…) → Create a new infobase → Next. Choose an infobase without a configuration for developing a new application, rather than another product’s demonstration configuration. Name it clearly, for example «Учебная сервисная служба». Choose local storage and a new directory, then complete the wizard. Exact labels can vary by version.

Keep experiments in your own infobase, distinguishable from other work.

Your training infobase appears in the list; selecting it shows its directory.

If the course infobase exists, compare its name and directory first. An empty customer list is not sufficient reason to create another infobase or replace an existing configuration.

5. Prepare the application in Designer

Launcher → select your training infobase → Designer

Verify that the selected row is your training infobase.

Choose Designer (Конфигуратор). If the tree is hidden, choose Configuration → Open configuration. Follow this lesson’s preparation, such as defining the simple Клиенты catalog or opening the application module. Introductory activities do not require loading the complete engineering template.

Designer changes the application definition; entering customer records is a separate activity.

The intended object properties or module editor shown in the lesson screenshot is open.

Preserve any existing source instead of replacing an entire module with an unrelated example. Use a separate new infobase when the first exercise requires an empty module.

6. Perform the task and run the version being checked

Designer → 1C:Enterprise

Preparation is complete and you have predicted the result.

After changing configuration code or structure, close its user application window. In Designer press Ctrl+S, then F7 to update the database configuration and confirm the intended changes. Start with F5. Enter customer cards in 1C:Enterprise; enter code inside the specified procedure in Designer. Changing ordinary customer records alone does not require F7 again.

The running application needs the new code or structure, whereas ordinary data writes already happen in user mode.

Observe the required list row, saved card, program message or report.

For old output, verify the infobase name, saved source and database configuration update. Do not open several simultaneous user sessions of one infobase in the training edition.

7. Compare and preserve your work

1C:Enterprise and Designer

The actions are performed or a specific mismatch has been found.

Compare actual and expected results. For cards, save and reopen the row. For calculations, preserve the module source and a screenshot of its message. To back up, close the application and use Designer → Administration → Dump infobase… with a new .dt filename. Test restoring in another new infobase while preserving the original.

Source, data, observations and backups serve different purposes; one displayed line is not the entire check.

The original work remains, observations can be shown and a backup has not replaced the source.

Restore .dt through 1C rather than importing it as Studio source. Never keep the only work copy inside temporary Windows.

8. Return to the Nexus self-check

Nexus → the same lesson

You obtained the practical result and preserved your deliverables.

Answer the questions and choose Check understanding. Attest the lab only after doing it yourself, then mark the lesson complete. For a mismatch, return to its step and preserve the observed difference; do not report an expected result as an actual one.

Separate understanding and your report from execution in the external application.

The attempt and completion belong to this course and content revision, awarding no automatic completion in the other course.

Nexus cannot see the external 1C window or automatically verify authorship. Reading theory alone leaves the actual practical run outstanding.

Optional: Studio, source transfer and isolated checks

Use this route when a lab explicitly requires project sources, file transfer or an isolated check. The first customer card and short calculation do not require it.
